page.layout: One printed page, two columns of running text: the main left column (biographical entries in italic and roman type, long s, large heading-like opening lines), and a narrow right column of dates and notes set beside it. No running head, page number, catchword or signature is visible in this part.; One block of handwritten text at the top of the page, with a printed mark "PRI" in the upper right corner; no printed margins.

main_text.p: Nicolaus Copernicus Torinensis Canonicus Varmiensis, natus anno 1473, Februa. die 19, hora 4, scrup. 48. Inclaruit maxime circa annum Christi 1525, post Ptolemaeum annis 1377 uel circiter.

Erasmus Reinhold natus in oppido Thuringiae Salfeld, praeceptor mihi carissimus & perpetua gratitudine celebrandus, qui & docuit et illustrauit haec studia multos annos in Academia Vuittebergensi magna cum laude felicissime, & praeclara ingenij monumenta reliquit, & plura reliquisset, nisi ab inchoatis operibus praematura eum mors abripuisset: hoc uersu uitam finijt.
Vixi et quem dederas cursum mihi Christe peregi.
main_text.head: Virg: 4. Georg:
main_text.p: Te nemiente die te decedente cambat

page.notes: Right column, read as marginal text: "1525 mortuus anno 1543." / "obijt in patria in complexu parentum suorum & liberorum 19 Maij anno 1553, Cū se Deo fiducia Christi meditatoris commendasset:" The right-hand column is set beside the text and is therefore given as a note here. Some letters in the scan are faint or broken; readings of the dates are as far as legible. The numbers in the main text (1473, 1525, 1377) are printed in a mixed notation and copied as seen. The upper right corner carries a printed or stamped mark "PRI" (a printer's or owner's mark, not transcribed as text). The text is written by hand in ink, with an underline in a brown or orange ink, and a bracket-like mark at the left of the second line. The handwritten line "Te nemiente die te decedente cambat" is transcribed as the scan shows; the letters are unclear and may be misread. Reference "Virg: 4. Georg:" is Virgil, Georgics book 4.
